title: Out of the darkness we have come to the highest light

words.context: Sāyaṇa: «तमसो विनाशकत्वेनोत्कृष्ट-», higher because it destroys the darkness

words.role: qualifies devam sūryam: ‘the god among gods’

sandhi.rule: t before v becomes d; m before t becomes n; visarga before p kept as s in this Vedic phrase
-aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o; -iḥ before a vowel becomes -ir

morphology.note: the root aorist of √गम् (classical would use the perfect or the a-aorist): ‘we have arrived’.
the comparative ‘higher’ and, at the end, the superlative uttamam ‘highest’: the verse climbs from one to the other.

translation.literal: Up beyond the darkness, seeing the higher light, we have come to the god among gods, the Sun, the highest light.
translation.readable: Looking up beyond the darkness to the higher light, we have reached the Sun, god among the gods, the highest light of all.

meaning: A single anuṣṭubh of ascent: from darkness to a higher light, and from that to the highest light, the Sun, ‘god among gods’. The verse is said by people who have come through darkness and now see the light above them. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (4.1.7.4) it is one of the verses of the fire-altar rite; Sāyaṇa takes the light there as the fire’s light which has become the Sun. In the Ṛgveda it is 1.50.10 (with the words of the first line in another order), in the great hymn to Sūrya whose first verse (ud u tyam) follows it in the rite. At midday it continues the upasthāna begun with ā satyena.
in_the_rite: Midday sūryopasthāna, the second of its five mantras (after ā satyena, before ud u tyam), recited standing and facing the Sun; it shares the viniyoga given for ā satyena in the Mylapore prayoga (vin-a-satyena).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on TS 4.1.7, reads the verse within the fire rite: the higher light is the fire’s, higher because it destroys darkness, and it is the same fire, now in the Sun, that ‘we have reached’ — «देवत्रा देवेषु मध्ये सूर्यं देवं सृर्यरूपेण वर्तमानमग्निसंबद्धमेवोत्तयं ज्योतिरगन्म प्राप्तास्म».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: He introduces it as the tenth verse of its series: «अथ दशमीमाह— उद्वयं तमस इति».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Anuṣṭubh. The Ṛgveda (1.50.10) orders the first line differently: «उद्वयं तमसस्परि ज्योतिष्पश्यन्त उत्तरम्» (‘seeing the higher light’ with jyotiḥ before paśyantaḥ). The phrase tamasas pari keeps s before p in both; the Taittirīya spelling joins the words (उद्वयन्तमसस्परि).

notes.label: direct
notes.text: The verse recurs in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa directly after drupadād iva (TB 2.4.4.9 and 2.6.6), the mantra the Mylapore prayoga recites at the āghrāṇa.
